::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 11th 1899  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Caroline Fairclough/31
:::

My dear [Mrs Butler](people/person_239.qmd)
At last I can send you the small amount for your [Snow Queen](other_books/otherbook_208.qmd) She was a long time waiting before I could get her in, but she looks very pretty in the number.

I had the pleasure of seeing [Grace Guinness](people/person_594.qmd) last month, and hearing of my dear [Lizzie](people/person_113.qmd), who is really a wonder, I wish [Emma](people/person_822.qmd) was as well![^1]

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

[Your husband](people/person_238.qmd) will be sorry to hear that the beautiful Common is being eaten up with houses, and there is talk of a Union Workhouse in the prettiest part.

---

[^1]: Grace (Butler) Guinness and Emma (Butler) Knight were her correspondent’s sisters-in-law;  Elizabeth Barnett was their aunt.
